questions.q: Match eyelid muscle with nerve and clinical sign in palsy — 1) Levator palpebrae superioris  2) Müller's muscle  3) Orbicularis oculi … A) CN III → Ptosis  B) Sympathetic fibres → Ptosis  C) CN VII → Lagophthalmos; Function A/B Elevation of upper lid, C Closure of eyelid
questions.exp: Table : Levator palpebrae superioris CN III Elevation of upper lid Ptosis; Müller's muscle Sympathetic fibres Elevation of upper lid Ptosis; Orbicularis oculi CN VII Closure of eyelid Lagophthalmos. (Book p206)

questions.q: Palsy of orbicularis oculi (CN VII) presents as ___, while levator/Müller's palsy presents as ptosis.
questions.exp: Orbicularis oculi CN VII Closure of eyelid -> Presentation in palsy Lagophthalmos. (Book p206)

questions.q: Match eyelid gland with type and opening — 1) Meibomian (tarsal)  2) Zeis  3) Moll … A) Modified sebaceous – Posterior to anterior surface of eyelid margin  B) Modified sebaceous – Base of lash follicles  C) Modified sweat – Base of lash follicles
questions.exp: Glands: Meibomian (tarsal) Modified sebaceous Posterior to anterior surface of eyelid margin; Zeis Modified sebaceous Base of lash follicles; Moll Modified sweat Base of lash follicles. (Book p206)

questions.q: Which gland opens posterior to anterior surface of eyelid margin?
questions.exp: Meibomian opens Posterior to anterior surface of eyelid margin; Zeis and Moll at Base of lash follicles. (Book p206)

questions.q: The grey line (gray line) divides the eyelid into ___ and posterior lamina.
questions.exp: Grey line : Divides eyelid into Anterior lamina and Posterior. (Book p206)

questions.q: Anterior lamina of eyelid consists of:
opts: Skin (thinnest skin in body), subcutaneous tissue, muscles
questions.exp: Anterior lamina : Skin : Thinnest skin in the body; Subcutaneous tissue; Muscles. (Book p206)

questions.q: Posterior lamina of eyelid includes: Tarsal plate has only fibrous tissue and:
questions.exp: Posterior : Tarsal plate has only fibrous tissue; Palpebral conjunctiva. Diagram labels Gray line, Zeis & moll glands, Meibomian gland, Eye lash. (Book p206)

questions.q: The cross-sectional eyelid diagram labels the grey line and glands. Which gland is most posterior?
questions.exp: Diagram : Gray line most superficial, Zeis & moll glands anterior, Meibomian gland deeper posterior tarsal. (Book p206)

questions.q: Match pathology — 1) Chalazion  2) External hordeolum / stye … A) Suppurative inflammation of Zeis gland  B) Lipogranulomatous inflammation of meibomian gland
questions.exp: Chalazion Pathology Lipogranulomatous inflammation of meibomian gland; External hordeolum Suppurative inflammation of Zeis gland. (Book p206)

questions.q: Infectivity comparison:
opts: Chalazion Non-infective, External hordeolum Infective : S. aureus
questions.exp: Infectivity Chalazion Non-infective; External hordeolum Infective : S. aureus. (Book p206)

questions.q: Match the swelling characteristic — 1) Chalazion  2) External hordeolum/stye … A) Painful diffuse swelling at the lid margin  B) Painless circumscribed swelling away from lid margin
questions.exp: Chalazion Painless Circumscribed swelling away from lid margin; External hordeolum Painful Diffuse swelling at the lid margin. (Book p207)

questions.q: Treatment for chalazion includes:
opts: Oral antibiotics alone for 7 days without incision (for stye)
Horizontal incision on posterior (conjunctival) lid + Intralesional triamcinolone
Hot compresses only with no incision or steroids
Cryotherapy to lash base with repeated epilation
questions.exp: Chalazion Rx : Incision & curettage : Horizontal incision on posterior part of eyelid (conjunctiva). Intralesional triamcinolone. (Book p207)

questions.q: Treatment for external hordeolum/stye is:
opts: Hot compresses, Oral antibiotics if recurrent
questions.exp: External hordeolum Rx : Hot compresses, Oral antibiotics if recurrent. (Book p207)

questions.q: Recurrence of chalazion should raise suspicion for:
questions.exp: Complications Chalazion Recurrence -> Sebaceous cell carcinoma. External hordeolum -. (Book p207)

questions.q: Hordeolum internum is:
questions.exp: Hordeolum internum : Suppurative inflammation of meibomian gland. (Book p207)

questions.q: Trichiasis is defined as inward misdirection of eyelashes that causes:
questions.exp: TRICHIASIS Inward misdirection of eyelashes Causes corneal opacity. (Book p207)

questions.q: Treatment for trichiasis — definitive vs periodic:
opts: Epilation every 1-2 months (periodic), Cryotherapy of lash base definitive
questions.exp: Treatment : Epilation every 1-2 months. Cryotherapy of lash base : Definitive. (Book p207)

questions.q: Match — 1) Entropion  2) Ectropion … A) Outward turning of eyelid margin m/c cause Senility  B) Inward turning of eyelid margin
questions.exp: Entropion Inward turning; Ectropion Outward turning m/c cause Senility. (Book p207)

questions.q: For entropion, management depends on type — Spastic, Senile, Cicatricial correspond to:
opts: Modified Wheeler/Weiss, Botulinum toxin, Modified Burrows/wedge
Botulinum toxin injection, Modified Wheeler operation / Weiss Operation, Modified Burrows operation / wedge resection
questions.exp: Entropion Rx : Spastic -> Botulinum toxin injection; Senile -> Modified Wheeler operation, Weiss Operation; Cicatricial -> Modified Burrows operation, wedge resection. (Book p207)

questions.q: For ectropion, operations listed are:
opts: Medial conjunctivoplasty and Buryon Smith operation
questions.exp: Ectropion Rx : Medial conjunctivoplasty; Buryon Smith operation (as printed). (Book p207)

questions.q: Distichiasis is an extra ___ row of eyelashes.
questions.exp: DISTICHIASIS Extra posterior row of eye lashes. (Book p208)

questions.q: Madarosis is loss of lateral ___ of eyelashes & eyebrow due to chronic rubbing of the eye.
questions.exp: MADAROSIS Loss of lateral 1/3rd of eye lashes & eyebrow d/t chronic rubbing of the eye. (Book p208)

questions.q: Tylosis is:
questions.exp: TYLOSIS Thickening of eyelid margin. (Book p208)

questions.q: Ankyloblepharon is:
opts: Fusion of eyelid margin of upper & lower lid, seen post trauma
questions.exp: ANKYLOBLEPHARON Fusion of eyelid margin of upper & lower lid. Post trauma. (Book p208)

questions.q: Congenital ptosis is due to defective development of:
questions.exp: CONGENITAL PTOSIS D/t defective development of levator palpebrae superioris. (Book p208)

questions.q: Clinical features of congenital ptosis include:
opts: Prominent extra upper lid crease with hyperactive lid movement
Absent upper lid crease + Lid lag on downgaze (lid fails to descend)
Lid retraction on downgaze with hyperactive descent
Normal crease with lid fully closing on upward gaze
questions.exp: Clinical features : Absent upper lid crease. Lid lag on downgaze : Failure of eyelid to go down on downward gaze. (Book p208)

questions.q: Treatment of congenital ptosis based on LPS function: Moderate / Fair vs Severe / Poor
opts: Moderate-Fair -> Frontalis sling, Severe-Poor -> LPS resection
Moderate-Fair -> LPS resection, Severe-Poor -> Frontalis sling Sx
questions.exp: Treatment table : Moderate LPS Fair -> LPS resection; Severe LPS Poor -> Frontalis sling Sx. (Book p208)

questions.q: A child with closed jaw shows ptosis, but on opening the jaw the ptotic lid moves up. Diagnosis as per book?
opts: Simple congenital ptosis alone without synkinesis
Marcus Gunn Jaw winking: trigemino-oculomotor synkinesis
Myasthenia gravis with variable fatigable ptosis
questions.exp: Marcus Gunn Jaw winking syndrome : D/t trigemino-oculomotor nerve synkinesis. Closed jaw -> ptosis Open jaw -> lid moves up. (Book p208)

questions.q: Marcus Gunn jaw winking is due to abnormal synkinesis between:
questions.exp: Marcus Gunn D/t trigemino-oculomotor nerve synkinesis. (Book p208)
